concepts.why: The presence of epidermal acanthosis, scattered necrotic keratinocytes, and band-like lymphohistiocytic infiltrate on lingual biopsy, along with the clinical presentation of whitish edematous lacy patches with erosions, are consistent with mycosis fungoides.
The presence of fibrinogen deposition along the basement membrane and the clinical presentation of whitish edematous lacy patches with erosions are consistent with pemphigus vulgaris.

The presence of a type AB thymoma and decreased IgG serum level are consistent with thymoma-associated multiorgan autoimmunity, which can present with various autoimmune manifestations, including mucocutaneous lesions.

The presence of whitish edematous lacy patches with erosions on the tongue and buccal mucosa, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal acanthosis and band-like lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, are consistent with lichen planus.

The presence of a thymoma and the clinical presentation of mucocutaneous lesions, along with the histopathological findings of fibrinogen deposition along the basement membrane, are consistent with paraneoplastic pemphigus.

rationales.F01: Oral erosions are common in pemphigus vulgaris and paraneoplastic pemphigus.
rationales.F05: Mediastinal mass is highly suggestive of thymoma-associated multiorgan autoimmunity.
rationales.F06: Lacy, white erosive lesions are characteristic of pemphigus vulgaris and lichen planus.
rationales.F09: Fibrinogen deposition along the basement membrane is a hallmark of pemphigus vulgaris and paraneoplastic pemphigus.
rationales.F11: Type AB thymoma is a specific type of thymoma that can be associated with multiorgan autoimmunity.
rationales.F12: A large, hypercapturing extrapulmonary mass is consistent with a thymoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a thymoma and the combination of oral erosions with fibrinogen deposition along the basement membrane, along with systemic symptoms such as weight loss and a mediastinal mass, support the diagnosis of paraneoplastic pemphigus.
